articleTitle: MaxEnt conductivities
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers

articleTitle: Internet design using parametric indices
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Internetworking standards have enabled designers of internets to use devices from multiple vendors. In the design of an internet, two of the major technical problems revolve around the optimum selection of links between nodes and the location of the root of the tree which spans the configuration. The tree and its root form a heirachy of branches which link all nodes in an internet such that no loop paths exist between nodes. This paper describes how an Internet Descriptor can be used to assess effects on performance and reliability of the location of the root and configuration of the tree in an internet. In the two design examples, internet trees are examined in terms of their compactness. Internet throughput, end-to-end transmission time, configuration balancing and cost are all directly related to the degree of compactness of the tree, as is shown.

articleTitle: Configuration optimization of spanning tree
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The IEEE 802.1D Spanning Tree algorithm operates autonomously in the nodes of an internet to ensure that no loop paths exist. The algorithm enables a particular bridge to be selected as the root and a logical tree imposed on the internet. The algorithm also allows the tree to be modified if internet links fail. Poor positioning of the bridge which will be selected by the algorithm as the root can result in an internet tree which is sub-optimal. The Internet Tree Analyzer, ITA, enables the effects of failure on the delays and the resilience of the internet failure to be investigated. Spanning Tree operation is outlined as background and then the methodology used in ITA is explained. An operational, campus-wide internet is analyzed to illustrate the applications and benefits of applying the method.

articleTitle: Omsetterbaan met voile kortsluitbeskerming vir navorsing van ‘facts’ -toepassings in die Suidelike Afrika-netwerk
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The advantages of FACTS (Flexible AC Transmission Systems) for electric power systems are shown. The development of a phase arm, with full protection against short circuits are shown. The phase arm can also be used for a wide variety of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Induction motor reactive power as a means of flux control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents a transputer based induction motor flux control method which is independant of machine resistance parameters and does not require flux transducers. The system is based on the fact that the reactive power consumed by an induction motor is a function of flux in the main magnetising circuit and the leakage paths. That is, flux amplitude may be found if inductances are known. The field orientation control is derived from control of the voltage vector. The computation method as well as experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Open-loop amplitude prediction in Meteor-burst communications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper introduces the use of the Early Fast Doppler (EFD) phenomenon as an amplitude predictor in Meteor-Burst Communications (MBC). EFD theory, predictions and measurements are presented. Statistical analysis of the results show correlations between EFD and trail characteristics which make forward predictions possible in an open-loop MBC system. Estimates of improved data throughput are given. A method of implementation is given which uses an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for trail classification and prediction.

articleTitle: Increasing the received signal to noise ratio in SSB radio channels through the use of analytic signal rooting
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper the method described by Schroeder et al. [1] is employed to halve the bandwidth of a speech signal. Such a “rooting” system was implemented and the results indicated that a doubling of the information carrying capacity of, for example, a SSB radio channel or an increase of 3 dB in the received signal to noise ratio is possible by employing practical filters. It is also indicated that “noise shaping” takes place and that the subjective increase in signal to noise ratio may even be more.

articleTitle: Subharmonic components in an asynchronous pwmscheme with digital pulse modulation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An asynchronous PWM scheme developed for a traction application is described. A method for calculating the resultant subharmonic voltages is described and results presented. These include the result of pulse quantization in the controller. The subharmonic content is shown graphically as a function of the modulating frequency ratio to establish the ratio at which subharmonic production may be neglected.

articleTitle: Design equations for narrow-band e-plane waveguide filters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Accurate equations are presented for the design of narrow-band E-plane waveguide filters. The equations are simple to implement and enable the designer to design filters with relative bandwidths from 0.2% to 2% in a fraction of the time needed for accurate numerical procedures.

articleTitle: An experiment in the synthesis of two stop consonants for the cochlear prosthesis
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Many researchers tend to employ analysis/synthesis techniques in the coding of speech for use in cochlear implants (bionic ear). In systems employing 6 or 8 electrodes, as in the system described in this paper, the non-linearity of the stop consonants suggests that other features may be utilized for their synthesis. An alternative strategy to analysis/synthesis, is the recognition/synthesis strategy, which is proposed in this paper. We propose a strategy in which a linear mapping of the speech spectrum onto the cochlea is used in the case of vowels, while non-linear recognition/synthesis is used in the case of the stop consonants. Such a strategy ensures that the stop consonants always sound the same and are thus easier for the patient to learn, provided that a correct recognition is performed. Very promising results were obtained and it even suggests the possibility of creating a natural sounding cochlear prosthesis.

articleTitle: The synthesis of a new DC-free code with asymmetrical runlength constraints developed with the ACH-algorithm
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: We present a new dc-free code suitable for use on binary asymmetrical channels. Write-once recording of optical discs is an example of a channel requiring asymmetrical runlength constraints. The new code was developed with the well-known Adler-Coppersmith-Hassner Algorithm. The detailed synthesis of the new code is presented, together with its error behaviour and power spectral density. We have previously found that dc-constrained codes which do not have finite memory are very difficult to develop with the ACH-algorithm.

articleTitle: Radar target recognition using multiple bounce scattering terms
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: One of the most successful approaches to radar target recognition is based on the down-range radar cross section (RCS) profile of the target. A feature of the down-range profile is that some peaks relate to interactions between structures, as opposed to direct specular scattering. We propose a new method using interaction (multiple bounce) terms to compute a truly rotation invariant feature for radar targets to be used for recognition. We think that it presents a more reliable way of classifying radar targets which would trouble other recognition methods.

articleTitle: Simulation of domestic consumer loads and voltage drop on LV distribution feeders based on data collected from load restricted consumers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This report presents the results of load simulations based on consumer data collected by Ron Herman of Stellenbosch University in 1989.

articleTitle: A study of factors affecting LAN bridge performance
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: As the traffic on a LAN increases, the response deteriorates and the rate of increase in the throughput also decreases. One of the most frequently used methods of alleviating the problem is to divide the LAN up into two or more LANs linked by bridges. This paper shows that a bridge may not necessarily improve the performance on LANs, but compound the problem. A LAN bridge atempts to limit traffic to those LANs linking the LAN of the source station and that of the destination station, but the bridge also introduces a delay, for packets passing from one LAN to the other. This may not give the improved performance that was expected from the bridge link. Several of the key load and device related factors, which must be considered in assessing bridged-LAN performance, are discussed. The causes and effects of the bridge discarding frames are also examined.

articleTitle: Columnar scanning: A method for enhancing data compression of images
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Digital data representing an image may be compressed in order to reduce the storage space required by the image. This data is a sequence of numerical information (bits), representing the image pixels scanned through in some order. This scanning order is usually Raster Scanning (left to right, top to bottom). Columnar Scanning is presented here as an alternative to Raster Scanning. Columnar Scanning has been found by the author to provide significant improvements on data compression ratios over Raster Scanning. This improvement is limited to data compression methods which use the relationships between adjacent data in the uncompressed source data; ie methods such as run-length-coding [1] and Lempel-Ziv-Welch coding [2]. It does not improve on such data-sequence-independent methods such as Huffman coding [3]. Columnar Scanning is completely lossless, it does not alter the image data in any way, but makes it more useful to a data compression method. Attention is given to how it improves the data compression of a small black and white image (512×256 pixels).

articleTitle: The design of an NX64K data transmission system based on multiple parallel ISDN U interfaces
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A brief overview of a new X.21 leased line data transmission system is presented. Section III discusses synchronisation of the parallel links to each other. Section IV covers an end to end block error detection scheme for the system and section V shows how this can be converted to a bit error measurement using interleaving. An example of channel modeling is presented in section VI to show how the interleaver design may be optimised under bursty conditions.

articleTitle: Phase effects in Meteor-burst communications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between predicted and measured early fast Doppler and body Doppler phase effects over a forward-scatter meteor-burst link. The theory and fundamentals of these effects are detailed and numerical predictions of their magnitude are made. A phase and amplitude measurement system operating over a forward-scatter test link between Pretoria and Durban, South Africa, is described. Measured results confirm that phase abberations due to early fast Doppler and body Doppler are not a major influence in meteor-burst channel comunications. The early fast Doppler frequency spread was 38.7 Hz (mean) and duration, 89.3 ms (mean). Body Doppler had a mean frequency spread of 1.5 Hz.

articleTitle: A simple generic rank finding algorithm for structural matrices
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A simple algorithm to determine the generic rank of a structural matrix is described. The algorithm uses symbolic Gaussian elimination whilst minimizing “disruptions”. Although a successful outcome is not guaranteed, the algorithm has been tested on a large number of matrices without a single failure. Its operation is explained via examples.

articleTitle: On dominant scales of 1D signals using a variant Haar wavelet
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper first introduces the relatively new wavelet transform. The simple Haar wavelet is concentrated on for several reasons: 1) ease of computation 2) speed of computation 3) ease of implementation in hardware. It is shown that the orthonormal Haar wavelet is unsuitable for accurate frequency classification of 1D signals. With the use of non-orthonormal Haar wavelets, very good frequency component results are obtained. A new integer based O(n) algorithm using wavelets is described which identifies spectral components which are frequency, spatially, and phase localized.

articleTitle: Radar target recognition with neural nets
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The improved capabilities of current radar systems have made it possible to characterise targets to such an extent that sophisticated automatic target recognition using radar data has become feasible. We assess this pattern recognition task and present a peak based approach to radar target recognition. The promise of this approach is verified with an experiment where actual radar data is used in the classification of three generic targets.

articleTitle: Maximum entropy conductivity estimation from airborne electromagnetic step-response data
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The airborne electromagnetic method is a geophysical remote sensing technique for mapping the electrical conductivity of the earth. The primary magnetic field of a transmitter is varied, inducing a current in the ground. If we model the earth as a series of electrically homogenous layers, the induced current flows initially in the uppermost layer and then diffuses downward and outwards.

articleTitle: Simulation program for stellenbosch university satellite (SUNSAT) power system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The University of Stellenbosch is currently developing a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) micro satellite for communication and mapping purposes. Since this will be the first South African developed experimental satellite, the project will also be used to gain new technology for future aerospace and satellite applications. This project is financially supported by a number of South African companies. This paper discusses the power system requirements and proposes solutions for the power system design on board the satellite. The paper includes the simulation and analysis of the power system requirements of the orbiting satellite. Power electronic converters to be used will include maximum power point tracking, battery regulation, bus regulation and distributed power conversion. The specification and designs of key components, i.e. the solar panels, battery and regulators are evaluated against the system requirements during a typical flight path. These simulations include all the different modes of operation of the power system in an orbit cycle.

articleTitle: Meteor-burst communications : A review
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Meteor-burst Communications (MBC) relies on a technology that has taken 60 years to mature. There have been many successful test and operational MBC systems installed. MBC systems have included point-to-point links, and both fixed station and dynamic vehicular networks. Available systems range from low data rate telemetry, through medium data rate message handling to high-speed conversational voice developments. This paper outlines previous done work in the field and describes current systems and technology under development. Future research and development avenues are indicated with particular reference to local contributions to the science.

articleTitle: Applying a transient suppression technique to emulate frequency hopping in channel simulators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A transient suppression technique is presented for utilisation in channel simulators which are required to simulate very low fading rates. The fading is simulated by driving specially designed narrow band digital filters with two independent random Gaussian processes, resulting in a Rayleigh amplitude and uniform phase distribution of any signal subjected to (i.e. multiplied by) the outputs of the fading filters. Transients appearing at a filter output as a result of an input sequence before time k=0, when the simulator is switched on, hamper the effective use of the simulators. In this paper a systematic procedure is developed whereby the transients can be eliminated by specifying the initial conditions of the fading filters to ensure a stationary filter output at time k = 0. It is shown that this simple but effective transient suppression technique may also be used to incorporate random Frequency Hopping (FH) in existing fading channel simulators. A well known “step-down” procedure is employed to calculate a matrix which is multiplied by a vector of independent, zero mean, unit variance, Gaussian random variables to obtain the initial conditions of the narrow band fading filters. In order to emulate FH, the proposed algorithm is not only applied during the initialisation period of the channel simulator, but is thereafter re-executed whenever the simulator is required to emulate channel conditions at the next hopping frequency. Results are included to demonstrate that the detrimental effects of frequency hopping in digital communication systems can indeed be effectively and realistically emulated by this algorithm, without any sign of unwanted transient effects.

articleTitle: Towards rapid computing of high order spherical harmonics and their use in meteor radiant mapping
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The computation of spherical harmonics of high order can be inconveniently slow, due mainly to the need to evaluate lengthy recurrence relations for associated Legendre polynomials. It is shown that significant savings in computing time can be achieved by letting the polynomials be represented by model functions obtained either (i) in closed-form, or (ii) from numerical processing of data retrieved from storage. The speed and accuracy of some models that have been developed are assessed in the context of applications involving the spherical transform, with particular reference to its use in meteor radiant mapping. The results show that options (i) and (ii) above both yield model harmonics which closely approximate those derived rigorously for all orders up to at least 256. In case (i) the effective computing speed may be increased by a factor of up to ∼ 6, depending on the maximum order involved, while in case (ii) a factor of ∼ 40 is attainable but this option is subject to the availability of sufficient storage (up to ∼ 4.5 Mbytes). Other models discussed are either slower, or yield less satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Near-end crosstalk modelling in the digital subscriber loop with application to line code comparison
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The importance of near-end cross talk in digital subscriber loops is reviewed. Three statistical models are examined for predicting the mean and standard deviation of the NEXT interference power from n disturbers. The Bradley model is selected as being most accurate with moderate computational complexity. A a set of measurements on multipair cable to obtain model parameters is described. Crosstalk coupling on 26 gauge cable is found to vary with f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.4</sup>, have mean at 80 kHz equal to -93.7 dB and standard deviation of 11.5 dB. The distribution of the loss in dB across pairs of disturbers is Gaussian. The model is applied to compare line codes for the digital subscriber loop at both the ISDN basic rate and at 800 kBit/s. The well known advantage of the 2B1Q code for basic rate ISDN is substantiated, lending confidence to the model. The 2B1Q code is also shown to have the greatest noise margin of common codes at 800 kBit/s.

articleTitle: On the design and application of a class of asymmetrically matched nyquist low pass filters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the simulation and application of a class of Asymmetrically Matched Nyquist Low Pass Filters (AMN LPF's). These filters have several advantages which make them particularly attractive for digital communications, eg. low intersymbol interference (ISI) and optimum post detection S/N ratios as a result of the perfectly AMN transmitter and receiver LPF pairs. Simulation results, design considerations and applications of the AMN LPF's are presented. Comparisons between these filters and the conventional Square Root Nyquist (SRN) LPF's are made.

articleTitle: An improved microwave intrusion detection system using a horn-lens fed shaped cylindrical reflector antenna
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper assesses the performance of commercially available systems, noting their strengths and weaknesses and proposes a novel system offering superior performance. The criteria defining the system performance are presented, with particular emphasis placed on an assessment of the volumes of detection. A novel volume of detection offering superior features is discussed along with the horn-lens fed cylindrical reflector antenna combination required to establish this. Comparative tests performed on the new system and a common system using a cheese antenna are given. It is shown that the new volume of detection offers substantial advantages in terms of the important system criteria. Several results from the field trial of the prototype are included to emphasise the substantial improvements, both financial and in performance, of the new system over commercially available systems presently in use.

articleTitle: Application of Meteor-burst technology in Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents Meteor-burst Communications (MBC) as a viable alternative to radio-telephone and satellite communications for rural environments. The basic principles of MBC operation are presented along with the system considerations for successful rural communications. The cost-effectiveness and performance of MBC systems in rural applications is presented. The M-LINK rural MBC system is described.

articleTitle: On a class of polyphase CAZAC sequences and their application in HF channel sounding
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes a class of polyphase sequences, viz the Perfect Squares Minimum Phase Constant Amplitude Zero AutoCorrelation (PS-MP CAZAC) sequences. Examples of the generation of typical PS-MP CAZAC sequences or codes are given. Some of the unique characteristics of the codes are illustrated, including their Constant Amplitude (CA) Fourier transforms, their complex time domain, phase trajectory and ideal periodic Zero AutoCorrelation (ZAC) function properties. Additional characteristics are the remarkable resemblance between the CAZAC sequences and CWFM chirp signals and the unique relationship between their instantaneous frequency and Fourier transform representations, resulting in the characteristic CA feature. It is shown that these sequences are periodically self-invertible and therefore constitute the optimum sequences for maximum-likelihood channel estimation. Finally, an alternative to the Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) or “chirp” HF channel sounder, namely the coded pulse channel sounder, employing the PS-MP class of CAZAC codes as opposed to the more commonly used maximal-length (PN) probing sequences, is proposed. Techniques to extract HF ionospheric layer height (or “range”) and velocity (“Doppler”) information from the phases of the complex cross-correlation components associated with the individual multipath components of the HF channel, are derived. The paper concludes with simulation results to verify the validity of the proposed HF channel sounding technique.

articleTitle: On the equivalence of singular-value decomposition and frequency-domain training methods for fractional-T spaced equalizers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the equivalence between a singular value decomposition (SVD) technique of obtaining the optimum tap coefficient vector of a fractionally-spaced equalizer (FSE) [1] and a frequency domain approach proposed in [2]. Simulation results are presented to illustrate some of the intermediate steps in the development of the optimal FSE coefficient vector according to these algorithms, as well as some results to prove the algorithms' validity in a typical communication environment. Limitations of the spectral equalization technique are pointed out and possible modifications to further improve its performance are highlighted.

articleTitle: Linear predictive speech coding at 2400 b/s
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper the salient design criteria are discussed for the developement of a full duplex 2400 bit/second LPC Vocoder. The results of intelligibility tests as well as tests including background noise are described. A frequency domain technique, to improve the quality of LPC-coded speech at 2400 b/s, is also discussed. The aim of the latter technique is to investigate the possibility of coding the prediction residual of a Linear Predictive Coder and still retain a coding rate of 2400 b/s. Use is made of vector quantisation of the DFTs of the prediction residual. The effect of different size code books on the mean square quantisation error is indicated. Compared to a CELP coder this is an interesting alternative, as CELP coders are normally not used below 4,8 kb/s.

Author Keywords: Low bit rate speech coding intelligibility test
frequency domain coding linear predictive coding

articleTitle: Subpixel accuracy in motion estimation for video coding
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Interframe techniques in digital TV and HDTV coding are powerful in performance but not yet well established. Different approaches are being developed to improve the accuracy and effectiveness of the prediction process. Among these, an effective technique is the evaluation of displacements with subpixel accuracy. The aim of this work∗ is indeed the analysis of this estimation accuracy for use in hybrid DCT coding schemes. The traditional block-matching algorithm has been generalized in order to take into account displacements of subpixel accuracy: 1, 1/2 and 1/4 pixel accuracies and different interpolation functions have been tested. The prediction error energy has been used to evaluate the performance of the estimation process. Furthermore the total performance has been tested considering also the increase in overheads for transmission of the motion vectors. An attempt to overcome the computational complexity of subpixel accuracies has also been made. Results have been obtained by simulating a hybrid coder in the case of constant quality coding.

articleTitle: Statistical modelling of frequency hopped VHF channels in an urban environment and error correction on the channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper we present experimental and analytical results obtained when applying Fritchman [1] partitioned Markov chains to model the error sequences of mobile and stationary frequency hopped VHF radio channels. These results were obtained from real time measurements on the abovementioned channels. The Markov chain channel models were applied to the system using four modulation schemes, namely FSK, DPSK, QPSK and 8-ary PSK. By using error distributions obtained from both the experimental measurements and the channel models, BCH [5] and Reed-Solomon [5] error correcting codes of various block lengths and information rates were investigated for this application. Interleaving was also investigated with regard to optimal depth and results are presented to show the effect of different interleaving depths on the block error rate.
